The facility uses a sequencing batch reactor performing activated sludge secondary treatment. There are three seperate reactors working is sequence performing equalization, biological treatment, and secondary clarification.
Biosolids are sent to an aerobic digester.

Approximately 150,000 gallons of digestate is dewatered three days a week primarily on a three belt two meter Ashbrook Belt Filter Press. A cationic polymer is added to the digestate onto the belt press. Filtrate is captured under the prese and drains back to the facility influent sump pit. The press produces cake between 15% and 18% solids.
Treated effluent is discharged into a 1-acre-foot lined polishing pond and then flows into one of two percolation basins.
The cake is loaded into roll off bins and is trucked to Engel and Gray in Santa Maria where it is composted and repurposed as fertilizer.
